arxiv-1508-07749.title: ROOT — A C++ Framework for Petabyte Data Storage, Statistical Analysis and Visualization
arxiv-1508-07749.creator: I. Antcheva, M. Ballintijn, B. Bellenot, M. Biskup, R. Brun, N. Buncic, Ph. Canal, D. Casadei, O. Couet, V. Fine, L. Franco, G. Ganis, A. Gheata, D. Gonzalez Maline, M. Goto, J. Iwaszkiewicz, A. Kreshuk, D. Marcos Segura, R. Maunder, L. Moneta, A. Naumann, E. Offermann, V. Onuchin, S. Panacek, F. Ra
arxiv-1508-07749.description: Abstract ROOT is an object-oriented C++ framework conceived in the high-energy physics (HEP) community, designed for storing and analyzing petabytes of data in an efficient way. Any instance of a C++ class can be stored into a ROOT file in a machine-independent compressed binary format.

arxiv-2004-03983.title: Units and 2 2 -class field towers of some multiquadratic number fields
arxiv-2004-03983.creator: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin, Abdelkader Zekhnini, Abdelmalek Azizi
arxiv-2004-03983.description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigate the unit groups, the 2 2 -class groups, the 2 2 -class field towers and the structures of the second 2 2 -class groups of some multiquadratic number fields of degree 8 8 and 16 16 . 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification 11R04, 11R27, 11R29, 11R37. 1.

arxiv-2212-03399.title: Utilizing Source Code Syntax Patterns to Detect Bug Inducing Commits using Machine Learning Models
arxiv-2212-03399.creator: Md Nadim, Banani Roy
arxiv-2212-03399.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Md Nadim, Banani Roy. Detecting Bug Inducing Commit (BIC) or Just in Time (JIT) defect prediction using Machine Learning (ML) based models requires tabulated feature values extracted from the source code or historical maintenance data of a software system. Existing studies have utilized meta-data from source code repositories (we named them GitHub Statistics or GS), n-gram-based source code text processing, and developer’s information (e.g., the experience of a developer) as the feature values in ML-based bug detection models.

arxiv-2310-17959.title: Constraining the growth rate on linear scales by combining SKAO and DESI surveys
arxiv-2310-17959.creator: Simthembile Dlamini, Sheean Jolicoeur, Roy Maartens
arxiv-2310-17959.description: Abstract In the pursuit of understanding the large-scale structure of the Universe, the synergy between complementary cosmological surveys has proven to be a powerful tool. Using multiple tracers of the large-scale structure can significantly improve the constraints on cosmological parameters.

arxiv-2311-17011.title: Pricing and hedging for a sticky diffusion
arxiv-2311-17011.creator: Alexis Anagnostakis
arxiv-2311-17011.description: Abstract We introduce a financial market model featuring a risky asset whose price follows a sticky geometric Brownian motion and a riskless asset that grows with a constant interest rate r ∈ ℝ r\in\mathbb{R} . We prove that this model satisfies No Arbitrage (NA) and No Free Lunch with Vanishing Risk (NFLVR) only when r = 0 r=0 .

arxiv-2403-09159.title: Basque and Spanish Counter Narrative Generation: Data Creation and Evaluation
arxiv-2403-09159.description: Abstract Counter Narratives (CNs) are non-negative textual responses to Hate Speech (HS) aiming at defusing online hatred and mitigating its spreading across media. Despite the recent increase in HS content posted online, research on automatic CN generation has been relatively scarce and predominantly focused on English.

arxiv-2408-05844.title: Photon Angular Momentum and Zero-Point Oscillations
arxiv-2408-05844.creator: Peter W. Milonni, G. Jordan Maclay
arxiv-2408-05844.description: Abstract Radiation from a localized, oscillating charge distribution can have angular momentum that cannot be explained in classical electrodynamics. We consider the simplest example—electric dipole radiation of a single photon—and show that this angular momentum is attributable to zero-point oscillations in unexcited states of the dipole source.

arxiv-2409-18115.title: Unique forbidden beta decays at zero momentum transfer Preprint: NT@UW-24-14
arxiv-2409-18115.creator: Chien-Yeah Seng 1,2, Ayala Glick-Magid 2,3, Vincenzo Cirigliano 3
arxiv-2409-18115.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chien-Yeah Seng 1,2, Ayala Glick-Magid 2,3, Vincenzo Cirigliano 3. We report an exploratory study of the 𝒪 ⁡ ( α ) \mathcal{O}(\alpha) structure-dependent electromagnetic radiative corrections to unique first-forbidden nuclear beta decays. We show that the insertion of angular momentum into the nuclear matrix element by the virtual/real photon exchange opens up the decay at vanishing nuclear recoil momentum which was forbidden at tree level, leading to a dramatic change in the decay spectrum not anticipated in existing studies.

arxiv-2506-10272.title: Collective Bargaining in the Information Economy Can Address AI-Driven Power Concentration
arxiv-2506-10272.creator: Nicholas Vincent, Matthew Prewitt, Hanlin Li
arxiv-2506-10272.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nicholas Vincent, Matthew Prewitt, Hanlin Li. This position paper argues that there is an urgent need to restructure markets for the information that goes into AI systems. Specifically, producers of information goods (such as journalists, researchers, and creative professionals) need to be able to collectively bargain with AI product builders in order to receive reasonable terms and a sustainable return on the informational value they contribute.

arxiv-2508-11879.title: Derivatives of padded Schubert polynomials through pipe dreams Thanks: The author was partially supported by NSF awards DMS-2231565 and DMS-1945212.
arxiv-2508-11879.creator: Hugh Dennin
arxiv-2508-11879.description: Abstract . In recent work, Hamaker, Pechenik, Speyer, and Weigandt showed that a certain differential operator ∇ \nabla expands positively in the basis of Schubert polynomials. For π \pi a dominant permutation, Gaetz and Tung showed an analogous positivity result holds for a dual differential operator Δ \Delta acting on π \pi -padded Schubert polynomials.

europmc-pmc9233709.creator: Shi Y, Zhang H, Huang S, Yin L, Wang F, Luo P, Huang H.
europmc-pmc9233709.description: Epigenetics is closely related to cardiovascular diseases. Genome-wide linkage and association analyses and candidate gene approaches illustrate the multigenic complexity of cardiovascular disease. Several epigenetic mechanisms, such as DNA methylation, histone modification, and

pmc-10569175.title: Automated, Consistent, and Even-Handed Selection of Active Orbital Spaces for Quantum Embedding
pmc-10569175.creator: Elena Kolodzeiski, Christopher J. Stein
pmc-10569175.description: A widely used strategy to reduce the computational cost of quantum-chemical calculations is to partition the system into an active subsystem, which is the focus of the computational efforts, and an environment that is treated at a lower computational level. The system partitioning is mostly based on localized molecular orbitals.

pmc-10737581.title: WHICH MEASURES OF STRESS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING?
pmc-10737581.creator: Kyle Bourassa, Avshalom Caspi, Terrie Moffitt
pmc-10737581.description: Stress and stressful events are associated with poorer health. There are multiple approaches to measure stress—from assessing subjective perceptions of stress to assessing the development of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)—and multiple periods that can be assessed across the lifespan. How might stress result in poorer health? One plausible physiological mechanism is accelerated biological aging, which precedes many poor health outcomes.

pmc-12471283.title: Impact of Discordant Antibiotics on Outcomes After Percutaneous Cholecystostomy for Acute Cholecystitis: A Retrospective Analysis of 184 PCC Patients
pmc-12471283.creator: Lauren Lahav, Nitzan Goldberg, Tamara Jiryis, Hadasa Cristo, Hagai Soback, Shmuel Avital, Yaron Rudnicki
pmc-12471283.description: Background: Antibiotic discordance in patients undergoing percutaneous cholecystostomy (PCC) for acute cholecystitis (AC) remains a debated issue. While empiric therapy aims to cover the most common pathogens, source control via PCC may play a greater role in clinical outcomes. This study evaluates the impact of discordant antibiotic treatment on patient outcomes.

pmc-13271389.title: From association to causation: a decision-aware framework for reproducible biomarker discovery and precision intervention design in the human gut microbiome
pmc-13271389.creator: AbdulAziz Ascandari, Suleiman Aminu, Rachid Benhida, Daoud Rachid
pmc-13271389.description: Human gut microbiome research has generated many disease associations, yet few translate into clinical applications. A central obstacle is not a lack of data, but the limited integration of causal reasoning, as most studies report correlations without establishing directionality, confounding control, or mechanistic evidence.

pmc-13550688.title: Genomic characterization of aggressiveness in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
pmc-13550688.creator: Nesrine Benanteur, Chiara Villa, Fabio Bioletto, Maria Francesca Birtolo, Daniel De Murat, Julien Masliah-Planchon, Victor Gravrand, Inès Lebib, Mounia Benkhellat, Robin Boezennec, Stéphanie Allassonnière, Franck Letourneur, Yoann Martin, Fidéline Bonnet Serrano, Julian Jacob, Valentin Calugaru, Max
pmc-13550688.description: BackgroundAggressive evolution of PitNETs is rare; metastatic spread is even more. Defining aggressiveness and malignancy is challenging, subsequently hard to predict, and to understand. The aim was to provide a molecular definition of aggressiveness using genomic approaches.MethodsPitNETs from 206 patients were included. Associations between 9 clinicopathological features of aggressiveness and PitNETs’ omics were explored.

pmc-13602259.title: ACTIVE problem solving: An action-oriented method for transforming Complex or Chaotic problems into verified reusable solutions
pmc-13602259.creator: Reeder Vermaak, Meelan Roopa, Sara Grobbelaar
pmc-13602259.description: In problem landscapes characterized by extreme uncertainty, traditional analytical problem-solving often fails because causal relationships only become visible through intervention. Additionally, valuable insights obtained during crisis response frequently remain unarticulated and risk being lost after stability is restored if they are not deliberately recorded.

uslaw-usc-t10-s1471.title: 10 U.S.C. § 1471 — Forensic pathology investigations
uslaw-usc-t10-s1471.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s1471.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 75 (Deceased Personnel); Subchapter I (Death Investigations). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority.— Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of Defense, the Armed Forces Medical Examiner may conduct a forensic pathology investigation to determine the cause or manner of death of a deceased person if such an investigation is determined.
